question.question: v7
question.asks: Will China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) formally approve purchases of Nvidia's RTX Pro 5500 by Alibaba, ByteDance, or other Chinese firms by January 31, 2027?
question.settles_on: Whether MIIT moves from signaling intent and collecting purchase plans to actually approving Alibaba's, ByteDance's and other Chinese firms' purchases of the RTX Pro 5500 (versus blocking, delaying or capping quantities), so that Nvidia can ship the product into China and book related revenue.

possible_answers.label: Yes
possible_answers.holds_when: MIIT formally approves by January 31, 2027, a purchase of RTX Pro 5500 chips by Alibaba, ByteDance, or another Chinese firm.

possible_answers.label: Ruled out
possible_answers.holds_when: After September 27, 2026, MIIT formally rejects all RTX Pro 5500 purchase plans from Alibaba, ByteDance, and other Chinese firms, or formally prohibits those firms from purchasing the chips. This rung holds when that, or any other decision against the event of rung 1 as a whole, or a formal abandonment or withdrawal of it as a whole, was made after 2026-09-27 and stands on 2027-01-31, and only when rung 1 does not.

possible_answers.label: Still open
possible_answers.holds_when: Neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds on 2027-01-31.

Ladder: rung 1 Yes: MIIT formally approves by January 31, 2027, a purchase of RTX Pro 5500 chips by Alibaba, ByteDance, or another Chinese firm. / rung 2 Ruled out: After September 27, 2026, MIIT formally rejects all RTX Pro 5500 purchase plans from Alibaba, ByteDance, and other Chinese firms, or formally prohibits those firms from purchasing the chips. This rung holds when that, or any other decision against the event of rung 1 as a whole, or a formal abandonment or withdrawal of it as a whole, was made after 2026-09-27 and stands on 2027-01-31, and only when rung 1 does not. / rung 3 Still open: Neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds on 2027-01-31.

The forecast is also rung 1: the reported MIIT intent is specific to these purchase plans, and the January 31 deadline leaves time for at least one approval. This is a forecast, not a claim that approval has already been established. Domestic-chip preferences and possible bundling or quantity limits could constrain purchases, but the evidence does not indicate a formal rejection or prohibition, and rung 1 requires approval of only one purchase.

articles.title: China may let Alibaba buy Nvidia's RTX chips, Information reports
articles.text:
China may let Alibaba buy Nvidia's RTX chips, Information reports
While Chinese AI developers rely on Nvidia for training frontier large language models, they are grappling with a persistent shortage of capable AI chips.
(Sept 28): The Chinese government has signalled it may allow companies such as Alibaba Group Holding Ltd and ByteDance Ltd to buy Nvidia Corp's new RTX Pro 5500 chips, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology recently asked some companies to report on their plans to purchase the high-end graphics processor released this month, including how many and what they would use the product for, The Information said. The ministry told some of the firms it intends to approve the purchases, it reported.
Washington bars Nvidia's most powerful accelerators from China, concerned they would propel the country's AI efforts and aid the military of a geopolitical ally. The RTX Pro 5500, however, is a processor intended mainly for graphics and simulations, though it can also support artificial intelligence (AI) services. Unlike Nvidia's top-of-the-line accelerators such as the GB300 series, it's built on older-generation processes and is designed to provide workstation computation at scale.
While Chinese AI developers rely on Nvidia for training frontier large language models, they are grappling with a persistent shortage of capable AI chips. They often employ a mix of semiconductors from both foreign and local suppliers. On Monday, stocks in AI chip firms including Shanghai Biren Technology Co and Cambricon Technologies Corp fell on fears that an influx of foreign product may dent local demand.
"China has been pushing quite hard towards domestic chip self-sufficiency, so Beijing potentially allowing Alibaba and ByteDance to buy another Nvidia chip suggests pragmatism," said Charu Chanana, the chief investment strategist of Saxo. "Domestic chips are improving quickly, but there are still gaps in performance, supply and the broader AI ecosystem that Nvidia can fill."
The US administration recently lifted restrictions on some Nvidia chips, though the products tend to be older-generation chips that have been sold in small quantities.

items.summary: The US government bars Nvidia's most powerful accelerators from China on national-security grounds, a restriction the article describes as still in force and distinguishes from the RTX Pro 5500, which is built on older-generation processes and is intended mainly for graphics and simulations rather than being a top-of-the-line accelerator such as the GB300 series.
